issues: The upper and lower 8x8 regions appear to use black, white, dark blue, and cyan together, exceeding the usual three opaque colours per NES sprite palette.
Both eyes are square white blocks with square pupils rather than convincingly round mechanical eyes.
The broad black middle band and heavy horizontal rims flatten the body into stacked rectangles instead of a squat barrel.
Perfect bilateral symmetry and identical vertical colour strips make the design feel static and fan-made rather than characterful Capcom work.
At 1x the face reads clearly, but the blue-and-cyan body details merge into narrow stripes with little useful volume.
fixes: Remove either cyan or dark blue so each 8x8 sprite region uses black plus only two body colours.
Clip one pixel from each corner of both white eye shapes to make compact round eyes; keep each pupil as a clean 1-2 pixel cluster.
Narrow the black bands above and below the eyes by one row and use that space to round the outer barrel silhouette.
Widen the body at its middle and taper the top and bottom corners by one pixel to create a clearer barrel shape.
Replace the mirrored cyan strips with one controlled highlight on the upper-left and a single blue shadow mass on the lower-right.
Offset both pupils one pixel toward the travel direction to add intent and Capcom-style personality.

issues: Black, white, bright blue, and dark navy coexist in the upper and lower 8x8 regions, exceeding the usual three visible colours per NES sprite palette unless wastefully layered.
The middle is dominated by a thick rectangular black band, making the eyes feel pasted onto the body rather than embedded in a rounded barrel shell.
The eye shapes and centered pupils are very rigid and square, giving the drone less of Capcom's lively mechanical character.
The perfectly mirrored blue-and-white striping feels decorative and modern rather than function-driven Mega Man enemy detailing.
The top and bottom contours are clean but overly box-like; the barrel volume is not strongly expressed at 1x.
fixes: Reduce the sprite to black, white, and one blue plus transparency; replace the dark-navy pixels with either black outline or the main blue.
Thin or interrupt the black eye band near its outer ends so the white shell remains visibly continuous around the face.
Cut one pixel from selected eye corners to make each eye rounder, and offset the pupils by one pixel to imply drifting toward Mega Man.
Widen the middle shell by one pixel per side while tapering the top and bottom corners more deliberately to strengthen the barrel silhouette.
Replace one pair of mirrored blue stripes with a compact vent, seam, or single highlight cluster using clean 2-3 pixel shapes.

issues: The middle black band is too massive and rectangular, making the face read like a modern icon rather than a lightly outlined Capcom sprite.
Both eyes are square white blocks with square pupils; they do not convincingly read as big round eyes at 1x.
The upper and lower body sections are nearly mirrored, producing a stiff, generic barrel instead of a characterful mechanical form.
The blue vertical stripes do not establish a consistent light direction or curved barrel volume.
The silhouette is clean but overly boxy through the sides and lacks the small contour accents typical of Mega Man enemies.
fixes: Reduce the central band to 1-pixel eye outlines and a thinner connecting bridge so black does not dominate the face.
Notch the outer corner pixels of each white eye and offset or reshape the pupils to imply roundness and expression.
Taper the lower body by one pixel per side or add a one-pixel side step to strengthen the barrel silhouette.
Consolidate the blue shading along one side, with a single small opposite-side highlight rather than matching vertical stripes.
Break the top-bottom symmetry with a one-pixel vent, seam, or underside propulsion detail while retaining the black-white-blue NES palette.

issues: The eye band is a heavy rectangular black slab, making the body look like three stacked boxes rather than one rounded barrel.
Both eyes read as square white blocks with square pupils rather than large round mechanical eyes.
The upper and lower panels are almost perfectly mirrored, giving the sprite a generic icon-like construction instead of Capcom-style characterful asymmetry.
Black, white, dark blue, and bright blue appear together within the same 8x8 regions, exceeding the normal three-visible-colour NES sprite palette.
The broad horizontal outlines above and below the eyes are visually heavier than the one-pixel contour work typical of Mega Man 2-3 enemies.
fixes: Merge the two blues into one NES blue so each 8x8 sprite region uses black, white, and blue plus transparency.
Remove the four corner pixels from each eye white and adjust the surrounding black by one pixel to suggest round eyes at 1x.
Reduce the eye band by one row and let the white barrel contour continue beside it, avoiding the stacked-box appearance.
Inset the upper and lower outer corners by one pixel and use stepped 1-2-1 curves to strengthen the barrel silhouette.
Offset one pupil by one pixel or vary a small side detail to add the lively, slightly asymmetrical expression common to Capcom enemies.

issues: The enlarged sprite appears 16x18 rather than the intended 16x16.
Black, white, bright blue, and cyan occur together within the same 8x8 regions, exceeding the normal NES limit of three opaque sprite colours plus transparency.
The perfectly mirrored construction and broad rectangular eye band feel more like polished fan art than an MM2/MM3 production sprite.
The middle band forms a heavy black box, weakening the barrel curvature and making the body read as three stacked slabs.
The cyan vertical strips create extra internal segmentation that becomes busy at 1x.
fixes: Remove two vertical rows, preferably one from the upper cap and one from the lower cap, to reach 16x16 without compressing the eyes.
Reduce the palette to black, white, and one blue; replace the cyan strips with white or blue so every 8x8 hardware cell is legal.
Cut back the eye-band corners by one pixel and let the white shell remain visible there to reinforce a rounded barrel silhouette.
Simplify each cap to one solid blue cluster with a small white highlight rather than alternating blue and cyan columns.
Introduce a subtle one-pixel asymmetry or directional flight detail while retaining the strong two-eye read.
